questions.text: How do you structure a mobile app so that new features can be added without breaking existing screens?

follow_up_suggestions.text: Which architecture pattern did you use, and how did it help in practice?
How do you keep shared components from becoming tangled?

scoring_rubric.2: Names a pattern without explaining how it applies
scoring_rubric.3: Separates UI, state and data layers with reasons
scoring_rubric.4: Explains module boundaries, testing and shared components clearly
scoring_rubric.5: Discusses trade-offs, migration from an older design and team conventions

questions.text: Tell me about a performance problem you found in a mobile app. How did you measure it and fix it?

follow_up_suggestions.text: What tool did you use to profile it, and what did the numbers show?
How did you check that the fix did not cause a regression?

scoring_rubric.3: Uses a profiler and measures before and after
scoring_rubric.4: Explains the root cause and checks for regressions
scoring_rubric.5: Also covers monitoring in production and lessons for the team

questions.text: How do you handle an API that changes while a mobile app is already in users' hands?

follow_up_suggestions.text: How do you coordinate that change with the backend team?
What happens to users who have not updated the app?

scoring_rubric.1: Does not consider older app versions
scoring_rubric.3: Uses backward-compatible changes and version checks
scoring_rubric.4: Plans a rollout with deprecation windows and monitoring
scoring_rubric.5: Explains contract testing, staged releases and clear communication with both teams

questions.text: Describe how you test a feature in a mobile app. Which tests do you write, and which do you leave to manual testing?

follow_up_suggestions.text: Can you give an example of a test that caught a real bug?
How do you keep UI tests from becoming slow or flaky?

scoring_rubric.2: Only manual testing or only unit tests, without reasons
scoring_rubric.3: Combines unit and UI tests with a sensible split
scoring_rubric.4: Explains the test pyramid choices and handles flakiness
scoring_rubric.5: Also covers device coverage, release testing and metrics on test health

questions.text: A feature needs to work when the device is offline. How would you design the data storage and sync?

follow_up_suggestions.text: Where would the data be stored on the device, and why there?
What happens when two edits conflict after reconnecting?

scoring_rubric.2: Stores data locally without a sync plan
scoring_rubric.3: Describes local storage and a simple sync with retries
scoring_rubric.4: Handles conflicts and partial failures explicitly
scoring_rubric.5: Explains the design trade-offs, data limits and how it is tested offline
